s0102.literal: Father Xundao—"Xun" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xiu."
s0102.idiomatic: On "father Xundao": the Southern Dynasties history reads Xiu for Xun.

s0103.literal: Summoned Yang as Minister of the Grand Storehouse—"Minister of the Grand Storehouse" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Minister of the Lesser Storehouse"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.
s0103.idiomatic: On "summoned Yang as minister of the grand storehouse": the Southern Dynasties history reads minister of the lesser storehouse; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.

s0104.literal: Summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander—the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "summoned as Palace Attendant and Army Commander."
s0104.idiomatic: On "summoned as scattered cavalry regular attendant and central army commander": the Southern Dynasties history reads summoned as palace attendant and army commander.

s0105.literal: Concurrently Right Army General—"Right" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Left."
s0105.idiomatic: On "concurrently right army general": the Southern Dynasties history reads left for right.

s0106.literal: Posthumous title Huan-zi—Zhang Senkai's collation note says the character "zi" is redundant.
s0106.idiomatic: On "posthumous title Huan-zi": Zhang Senkai's collation note holds that zi is superfluous.

s0107.literal: Present review: Yang was first enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county; in Taijian year 12 he was stripped for dealings at the frontier; when Emperor Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—writing "zi" here does not fit; Zhang is correct.
s0107.idiomatic: Present review: Yang was first made marquis of Dingxiang; in Taijian year 12 he lost his title for frontier dealings; when Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—so zi here is wrong; Zhang is right.

s0108.literal: At that time Master Lang of Xinghuang Monastery was thoroughly versed in the Buddhist canon—"Master Lang" in Yuan Gui 821 reads "Master Huilang."
s0108.idiomatic: On "Master Lang of Xinghuang Monastery, thoroughly versed in the Buddhist canon": Yuan Gui 821 reads Master Huilang.

s0111.literal: [Cui] the sharp point and repel the enemy—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0111.idiomatic: On "[crush] the vanguard and repel the enemy": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
